requirements-nfr.decision: Take over the binding-constraint and scope questions from architecture-core, and set the quality bar for the parity test: which surfaces it must cover (skill, methodology, agenda writer, deployed copies), what counts as a second definition, and what its failure message must say.

architecture-core.decision: Your carried question: how iteration 1 orders whole lenses when a mixed lens (data-storage, security-compliance, integration-api, ui-ux, devops-operations) still asks solution questions before architecture-core in a single pass; and whether consumers read index.yml at runtime or keep copies that the parity test checks.

data-storage.decision: The shape of the space tag in index.yml (field name, values, whether 'mixed' exists, how a one-space lens says so) and whether a confirmed agenda records the order it was confirmed under, for FR-013 migration.

devops-operations.decision: Which deployed copies the parity test checks (squad-templates skill, host skill copies, downstream lens catalog), and how specrew update carries the new order to existing projects without changing a mid-workshop agenda.

code-implementation.decision: Craft rules for the PowerShell/Pester changes: the parity test's shape and location, reading index.yml without a new dependency, and recording the reviewer host you choose below.

skipped.component-design: No new component boundary: the change is lens text, the index.yml catalog, one test and the order an existing writer uses; the consumption model is decided in architecture-core.
skipped.ui-ux: No screen or visual state; the workshop's conversational order is the subject itself and is decided in architecture-core.
skipped.security-compliance: No identity, secret, sensitive data or new trust surface; the edits are lens text, a YAML catalog and a test.
skipped.integration-api: No external contract or protocol; index.yml is an internal catalog whose shape is covered in data-storage.
skipped.observability-resilience: No runtime behaviour to observe beyond the parity test's failure message, whose wording is set in requirements-nfr.

requirements-nfr.decision: Binding: index.yml sole order source; FR-013 no confirmed agenda changes; single pass; gate readers of Design Decision Points keep working (with a test); 203/pin/b4f-142 untouched; 204 reserved; deployed copies sync-produced only. Scope as proposed. FR-001 option b: known surfaces plus sweep of shipped text only (specs/ and proposals/ never scanned or rewritten); relative-order match passes so subsets need no exemption; exemptions state a reason and are shown to the human; deployed copy differing from source fails with run-the-sync message; agenda writer refuses relative-order violations for new agendas, never reorders, pre-release agendas exempt. FR-005 checks a/b/c; section shape decided in data-storage. Failure output names file:line, expected and found order, fix, and reports every mismatch in one run.

architecture-core.decision: Order option A (product-domain, requirements-nfr, ui-ux, security-compliance, data-storage, integration-api, devops-operations, architecture-core, component-design, observability-resilience, code-implementation) with the problem section asked first inside every lens; no formal decide-later in iteration 1 (deferrals stay in decision text). Consumers: agenda writer reads index.yml at runtime; prose lists kept and parity-checked; skill gains the sentence that index.yml wins on disagreement. No new structure; catalog is the volatile point. Amends requirements-nfr: full lists (skill list, methodology catalog tables, catalog README) must match index.yml exactly in order and membership; relative-order rule for partial lists only; the test names the full surfaces.

data-storage.decision: index.yml gains space: problem|solution|both; list position is the order; tags as proposed (problem: product-domain, requirements-nfr; solution: architecture-core, component-design, observability-resilience, code-implementation; both: ui-ux, security-compliance, data-storage, integration-api, devops-operations). Lens files: ### Problem questions / ### Solution questions inside ## Design Decision Points, with an extractor test; a bullet mixing both spaces is split into two bullets keeping words and meaning, every split listed in the plan. FR-013: no new field; order check only at confirmation; test proves old confirmed agenda resumes. Scope amendment (original text kept): iteration 2 = problem-space completeness with its own short workshop; iteration 1 lists problem-side gaps per lens while tagging; iteration 3 = back-check, amendments, sweeps after 203.

devops-operations.decision: Failure message names the two project-only deploy scripts (deploy-speckit-extension -RefreshExisting, deploy-squad-runtime), never the full update; scratch verification showed they refresh every checked copy incl .cursor and also restamp .squad runtime files (message says to review git status); real-home hook files unchanged (correction: ~/.specrew/hook-bindings/ folder exists, untouched by mtime, included in future checks). specrew-update.ps1 never run in this worktree while 203 unmerged. Copy comparison: full content of touched files minus deploy wrapper. CI: named step in specrew-ci.yml; markdownlint (CI command) before every push, no push on non-zero; follow Specrew CI, Test, Cross-Platform Validation to conclusion after every push, skipped gate = red. Skill sentence gains: a confirmed agenda keeps the order it was confirmed in. Rollback = revert in next beta.

code-implementation.decision: Repo conventions (script-style tests, existing refusal helper), no other guideline; PowerShell 7, all baseline defaults on. Test-first lens-order-parity.tests.ps1 + extend workshop-agenda-confirmation.tests.ps1; run every existing workshop test locally and report; register as named specrew-ci.yml steps the two files plus every existing workshop test covering a touched file that passes; already-red workshop tests reported as findings, never fixed or omitted silently. Refusal via New-SpecrewWorkshopAgendaRefusal, never reorder; parity test collects all mismatches. No new dependency; Read-IntakeYaml verified to parse the space scalar (scratch copy). Reviewer codex, authorized workshop-205-workshop-lens-order.
